next_row.boundary_rationale: A first-person report, “From the uttermost part of the earth have we heard songs.” gives way inside the same verse to personal lament: “I pine away! I pine away! woe is me!” (web:Isa.24.16), matching א֣וֹי לִ֑י (oshb:Isa.24.16, byte tier) — the distinct אוי lexeme, a different word from the woe-series onset lexeme used elsewhere in this book. The verse closes on treachery, בֹּגְדִ֣ים בָּגָ֔דוּ (oshb:Isa.24.16, byte tier), which threads without a fresh scene marker into the terror imagery of Isa.24.17-20 (“Fear, the pit, and the snare” web:Isa.24.17; “The earth will stagger like a drunken man” web:Isa.24.20). That internal continuity is tested by a second-person-masculine-singular addressee marker opening Isa.24.17, עָלֶ֖יךָ יוֹשֵׁ֥ב הָאָֽרֶץ (oshb:Isa.24.17, byte tier) — “Fear, the pit, and the snare are on you who inhabit the earth.” (web:Isa.24.17) — which turns the terror catalogue toward direct address of the same collective subject the chapter has held in view throughout, before Isa.24.18-20 revert to third-person description; the material is read as threading on through this turn because the same scene and interlocutor persist across it, but the shift from first-person lament to second-person address is disclosed rather than smoothed over. This span carries a WEB continuation-paragraph fold, a tier-4 layout signal beginning at Isa.24.16, that does not itself argue the row's bounds. The row's own close, before Isa.24.21, is driven by the day-formula onset וְהָיָה֙ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֔וּא (oshb:Isa.24.21, byte tier) — the sole day-formula site in this chapter, and the same onset class the neighboring units in this range treat as a tier-1 driver — rather than by the setumah (single-witness) following oshb:Isa.24.20, which corroborates the edge at tier-3 without driving it.
